blocks.summary: The abstract states the position that interleaved images do not appear to drive current thinking-with-images performance gains.
The introduction motivates thinking with images and sets up the question of whether intermediate images are necessary.
The paper formalizes thinking with images as a sequence where each step may be text or an interleaved image.
Table 1 reports that suppressing interleaved image outputs causes little performance degradation.
Table 2 shows raw Qwen3-VL and thinking-with-image Qwen3-VL perform essentially the same on HRBench.
Figure 2 visualizes attention maps, showing answer-token attention mostly on original images.
Table 3 compares DeepEyes-7B with a simple SFT baseline without interleaved images.

blocks.section: Call to Action and Alternative Views
blocks.summary: The paper calls for interleaved-image ablations, tools that add new information, and harder benchmarks.
The conclusion restates the need for mechanistic transparency and better visual reasoning benchmarks.
Table 5 combines better context and better prior with Hide on V*.
Figure 1 illustrates the ideal thinking-with-images workflow.
